summary: Sends full DAT tables across the network to a Touch In DAT in another TouchDesigner process, providing a high-level table synchronization mechanism.

key_params.name: protocol
key_params.note: Streaming TCP/IP, UDP messaging, or multicast UDP transport

key_params.name: address
key_params.note: Destination or multicast address used by the selected protocol

key_params.name: port
key_params.note: Network port used for outgoing packets

key_params.name: shared
key_params.note: Share a connection with other networking DATs using the same protocol

key_params.name: redendantsends
key_params.note: Maximum consecutive redundant sends of the same data

key_params.name: resend
key_params.note: Send current data immediately regardless of prior sends

key_params.name: messages_pending
key_params.note: Pending network message count for diagnostics

key_params.name: customext
key_params.note: Custom editor extension when extension mode uses a custom extension

common_gotchas: Touch Out DAT sends full table contents to Touch In DAT, not individual event messages.
Use Redundant Sends and Resend deliberately; they can help late or lossy receivers but increase traffic.
The output network target must match the receiving Touch In DAT protocol, address, and port.
Active off stops sending; it does not queue table changes for later delivery.
For ad hoc text or binary messages, UDP Out DAT or TCP/IP DAT is usually the more direct tool.
key_concepts: Touch Out DAT sends whole DAT tables to a Touch In DAT peer in another TouchDesigner process.
Redundant Sends and Resend Data control repeated table transmission for receiver reliability.
Protocol, address, port, and shared connection settings define the receiving endpoint.
It is intended for table synchronization, not general packet/message transport.
